messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a 3x SLO violation spike at ~03:12 UTC during the GPU hibernation window in us-west-2. Token tail latency jumped, lots of queued requests. Looks correlated with scale-to-zero wakeups. Anyone else seeing startup jitter? @samir @lin
samir: On it. Do we know if traffic hit cold nodes or fell back to a smaller model? Any logs/trace ids?
lin: Traces show routing to 'economy' pool which uses aggressive scale-to-zero. Node startup time was ~45s in the traces; driver init + cuda setup ~30s. KV cache warmup also added ~10-12s.
chen: We dropped the keepalive from 180s -> 60s last week to save GPU hours. That probably made cold starts more common across low-traffic AZs. Suggest bump back to 180s and add randomized cooldown jitter per node.
ashley: Quick cost check: raising baseline from 60s->180s across fleets estimates ~+2% GPU hours monthly (ballpark). For SLOs that seems acceptable, but confirm ops budget.
ops-bot: Notice: policy-change candidate detected — throttler.cooldown was modified 14m ago by @chen in staging. CI: passed, smoke: failed (1/12) — see https://ci.internal/reports/2345
maya: Can we run a controlled canary? Target us-west-2, 10% traffic, validate end-to-end latency and KV cache warm numbers. If it reduces SLO spikes, we roll.
samir: I'll prepare canary. Plan: patch autoscaler policy for a single nodepool and route 10% via header override. Command I'll run: ``kubectl apply -f canary/scalepolicy-usw2-canary.yaml``
lin: Also add a tiny pod-level startup probe to measure cuda init time and surface as metric `gpu_init_ms`. Patch example: ```kubectl patch nodepool gpu-usw2 -p '{"spec": {"template": {"metadata": {"annotations": {"probe/gpu-init": "true"}}}}}'```
chen: After canary, watch: node boot time, gpu_init_ms, kvcache_warm_ms, and model-fallback count. If kvcache_warm_ms > 20s we probably need a prewarm job to prime caches.
ashley: Scheduling canary for 02:00 PT tomorrow — ops budget approved. I will allocate warm capacity for the window.
maya: Thanks. If canary looks good, let's also add a temporary safety net: increase fallback model capacity so requests don't pile on cold GPUs during transition.
samir: Will update the routing policy to prefer fallback at 60% load threshold for the canary. Posting dashboard links after run.
chen: FYI we should also add jitter to the drain cooldown to avoid synchronized wakes across AZs; +random(0..90s) should help.
maya: Awesome — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
